changes.evidence: The first low character has an open n-like turn rather than a closed o. Its long low continuation ends below a separate dot, which belongs to i. This supports ni, as in H.
Following ni are exactly two short horizontal levels. The lower begins with a small pen turn, but there is no independent m or the letters of même.
The subscript is one U with a rounded lower basin and a wavy mark above it. There is no second O subscript below U; H adds an extra level.

The subscript has a long left stem descending to a sharp low vertex, a rising oblique branch and a returning right leg. The same sharp shape is present in the K of deg tr K on this leaf, while the opening U has a rounded basin. K is preferred, with U retained as a shape alternative. No other leaf was used for this comparison.
The only mark to the right of the small s is its raised/sloping prime. There is no second independent comma after it.

The first word has the crossed tall t, low r/i/v strokes and tall final l. The second starts with tall k and successive low u/m forms; a separate short oblique mark above the e is distinct from the later i-dot. The letters and length do not support maximal.

Below the live simeq is a dark small oblique oval-like form crossed by an overworking stroke, with a short upright and a tiny separate right trace. Neither witness records it. Its original identity cannot be recovered. The draft preserves it as an uncertain cancelled sublabel; the question mark is an editorial placeholder, not a source question mark. Even the exact deletion state remains less secure than the presence of the extra ink.
The word deg has a looped d and descender g; a separate tall t/r form follows, then a large angular K, the short minus, and 1. These are several written units, not a single n.

The word de is separately visible. The following large angular form has a high right stroke and a deep return, without a small zero below it. This does not support k_0. N remains a doubtful reading because the letter is highly cursive and the lower return is unusual.

The subscript repeats the sharp low vertex, rising oblique and returning right leg seen in the first N-identification and in the K of deg tr K. It differs from the rounded basin of opening U. K is preferred with an explicit U alternative.
After the dash are a low m, a small closed a, the detached i-dot, and the separate final s; the next word is the looped d/e form de. There is no tall d at the start of dirais and no j descender.

The first word starts with d/e, continues through the compressed u/x and dotted i, and has the accented e before the final low m/e. A single independent underline lies below it. The next word has a long p descender and the remaining espèce strokes, followed by a stop. This is not the short word pire.

Between Une and autre is a tall overworked beginning with upper and lower loops and crossing strokes, consistent with an abandoned f. A fresh complete façon follows autre. The word autre lies on the main writing line and has no separate insertion leader. The abandoned letter is retained as doubtful, rather than treating autre itself as an insertion.
U is physically above S, with a distinct horizontal separating bar. The source uses a stacked fraction, not an inline slash.

A first p-shaped descender and a terminal tall stroke are joined by a heavy horizontal cancellation. A second, live peut follows. The cancellation obscures the internal letters of the first word, so the C doubt remains.
The letters after the p/a/r/c/o sequence run through a compact u/r into one tall terminal t. There is no additional a/n sequence before that final t.
After the tall l and separate apostrophe are a low e-like turn, an n hump, and a trailing s return. No abbreviation point is written.
The final S has its complete upper and lower curves. The small area to its upper right is blank; no separate prime is present. No terminal stop is supplied.
A distinct faint marginal hand writes a looped 9 with a descending tail followed by an oval 0 in the bottom-left corner.

The small oval below the wavy mark has no rightward sigma exit stroke. It is O.

A short oblique accent before the i-dot is distinct from that later dot, supporting the accented e in kummérien.

The cropped word contains the tall crossed t, compressed r/a/n, separate s/c forms, a low e/n run and the following tall d, with a compressed final ance. The word reaches its end within the paper edge.
The angular form has a high stroke and deep return but is too cursive for certain identification. There is no distinct small 0 as required by H’s k_0.

notes:
This page continues a discussion of a section and a subgroup N_s-prime. It says that the subgroup gives almost a lifting, with the inertia factor T still obstructing it, and that a section of the indicated extension gives a section of the special-fiber group, but of the second kind. It then begins another formulation in terms of a rational section f of U/S and the family of points f(s) in the fibers U_s. The final sentence continues beyond this sheet. The underlined words presque and deuxième are the author’s qualifications. The page bears his number 45 and the separate bottom-left folio 90.
Visual review: the whole source image was viewed once, then both full-resolution halves once, comparing every word, formula, sign, subscript, cancellation, underline and placement with C and H. Twenty-two distinct saved crops were inspected once. Original boxes are recorded; crops used grayscale autocontrast, LANCZOS resizing to 2200 pixels width and sharpening. No OCR, text-recognition software, external research, or other leaf was consulted. The line count is twenty main prose rows, excluding the page and folio numbers. There is no diagram or drawing on this leaf.
Reading decisions: the opening is ni =, with the equals sign kept literally. Opening E_tilde U has a rounded U, and the following subscript is O. The two N-identifications instead have the sharp low vertex, oblique rise and returning right leg of the K in deg tr K on this same leaf; K is preferred with U retained as an explicit alternative. No independent comma follows the first N_s-prime. The words trivial kummérien, transcendance, obstrue, tous, cette, mais de deuxième espèce, and parcourt l’ens are supported by their crops. The accent in kummérien is separate from its i-dot. The source fraction U/S is stacked. The final S has no prime, and the final sentence has no supplied terminal stop.
The small overwritten form below the first simeq is newly preserved as an uncertain cancelled sublabel. The question mark used inside the doubt macro is an editorial placeholder for its unknown identity, not a claimed author question mark. A doubtful abandoned f-like start precedes inline autre; autre itself is not raised or attached by an insertion leader. The struck word before the live article, the live le/de, the letter N after corps de, and the struck peut remain doubtful. The exact state of the tiny sublabel remains less secure than its visible presence. Certainty-only resolutions have their own list and marks; they are not substantive change rows.
Mathematical checks: no independent proof, computation, refutation or mathematical use was performed. The same-page comparison of K and U is a handwriting comparison, not a mathematical check. check_events is therefore empty. No compilation was performed.
